hook.text: Whiteout erases the horizon—sky and surface merge into featureless white, and spatial orientation vanishes.

buildup.text: It occurs when snow cover and overcast skies create uniform lighting—shadows disappear and depth perception fails.

discovery.text: Pilots lose the ability to judge altitude or attitude visually—a potentially fatal loss over flat, snow-covered terrain.

twist.text: Whiteout also occurs in blowing snow—reducing surface visibility to zero even without any precipitation falling.

climax.text: The 1979 Erebus crash in Antarctica killed 257—the aircraft descended into a volcano in whiteout conditions.

punchline.text: Everything looks the same—and that's exactly the danger.

quiz.question: Why is whiteout dangerous for pilots?
options: The horizon disappears, eliminating visual orientation cues
